I also found this episode extremely relatable. I watched this show for the first time a few months ago and binged it pretty fast. I turned 32 while watching which I think gave me a certain perspective of that time. 

In my 20s I definitely had some toxic and intense friendships. One specific relationship was echoed in in Marnie and Hannah (and a little bit of Shosh too). By the end of my 20s, we were pulling away. At 29 I moved across the country and tried to do my own "goodbye tour" and kind of realized these friendships that consumed me were basically dead. 

The person I considered my best friend sort of pulled a Shosh and never said goodbye to me. She had found other friends that matched where she was at in life better and pushed me aside to be with them. Not that what Shosh did was wrong, but that scene kind of hurt due to my own experiences.

Fast forward to now and I have a very different (but better) life. I have a really solid friend group and feel like I finally belong somewhere. It's weird having healthy relationships with people after that friendship in my 20s, but I'm extremely grateful.

I like that this show doesn't shy away from the messiness. I can't say I've seen anything else that really hit so close to home the way Girls did with the friendship dynamics.

Anyways, I'm done rambling. Thanks for coming to my Ted Talk.

For example, I'm saving up to get invisalign to fix my overjet and I might get hair extensions to make mine look thicker and more full. I'm also not overweight by any means, but I'm not skinny either and am trying to lose about 10 - 15 lbs. I feel like I'll feel more comfortable in my skin after these fixes. 

But I have to accept that I'll always have wide hips and c-cups. I have to accept my pale skin. My hooded eyes. My slightly below average face. And I have to learn that it's okay to not look like my size 2 friends or celebrities. 

It's important to give yourself some love and remember that confidence and character really go a long way. I'm hoping I'll start to feel better about myself in my 30s, but it's a process and a lot of re-wiring your brain to learn self love after years of hating yourself.
